findings.issue_text: [BUG] gen_request_data compares ErrorEvent['timestamp'] values (which come from nodestore event payloads via data.get('timestamp', 0.0) at line 115 and are ISO-8601 strings like '2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') against replay segment event timestamps (numeric epoch milliseconds), so the comparison raises TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'float' despite the TypedDict declaring timestamp: float. Every summarize-breadcrumbs request for a replay that has at least one error event and any recording segment raises an unhandled TypeError inside paginate's on_results and returns a 500 instead of the AI summary — the feature's primary path is dead on arrival.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs each error_id with the positionally-i-th value of nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)'s returned dict via zip, but get_multi's dict iteration order follows queryset result order (DjangoNodeStorage) / thread-completion order, not the requested node_ids order, so an ErrorEvent's id is zipped with a different event's payload. On the default Django nodestore backend (and any backend that returns missing keys unordered or omits them, which also shifts the None-filtered positions), the AI breadcrumb summary reports the wrong titles/messages for the replay's errors — wrong error content is fed to the model and shown to users, with the mispairing growing worse the more errors a replay has.

[BUG] The endpoint now calls self.get_filter_params(request, project), which requires statsPeriod or start/end query params and raises ApiBadRequest when they are absent, where the previous implementation of this GET endpoint consumed no date-range params at all. Any existing caller of the summarize-breadcrumbs endpoint that does not send a date range (i.e., every caller written against the old contract) now receives a 400 ApiBadRequest instead of a summary; only clients updated in lockstep with this change keep working.

[ADVISORY] The query_replay_instance snuba RPC is executed unconditionally on every summarize request, but its only consumer is the error_ids list, which is discarded when enable_error_context=false (the disable flag skips only the nodestore fetch at line 94). Callers who pass enable_error_context=false still pay a full extra snuba replay-instance query per request whose result is thrown away, and every caller gains unconditional snuba load/latency on a path that previously made no snuba calls — operators of high-traffic orgs see added snuba QPS with no way to disable it short of a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] Deleting the regex-experiment dispatch branch orphans the _handle_regex_match callback (the only call site was the removed experiment.run(content, _handle_regex_match)), leaving dead code in the ingest-critical grouping parameterizer. The next change to grouping parameterization must reason around a callback for an experiment class that no longer exists, and anyone re-adding a regex experiment will pattern-match on code that is provably unreachable; the function and the removed isinstance branch should have been deleted together (passes the deletion test: both the callback and the branch become unnecessary).

[ADVISORY] get_environment_info performs a per-issue issue.get_recommended_event() lookup (eventstore query plus nodestore fetch) inside the merged-PR comment loop, and wraps it in `except Exception` logged at info level. Each merged-PR comment generation for N linked issues adds up to N sequential recommended-event round trips to a path that previously made none, and any failure in that lookup is swallowed at info level so environments silently missing from PR comments are invisible to operators debugging why environment info never appears.

[BUG] MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE embeds the unescaped, truncated issue title inside markdown link text ([**{title}**]({url})), whereas the old template kept the title outside the link, and CommonMark refuses to parse a link whose text contains an unbalanced ] or [ — which the error-message titles this feature surfaces (e.g. "Unexpected token '['", "Index out of range]") commonly contain. Merged-PR comments for issues whose titles contain an unmatched bracket render as literal raw markdown text instead of a clickable issue link, degrading the GitHub/Gitlab PR comment for exactly the noisy error titles this workflow exists to surface.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results via zip(error_ids, events.values()), but nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict containing only the node ids that were found, so the two sequences misalign whenever any error event is missing from nodestore. For any replay where at least one error event has been purged from nodestore (retention, deletion), every subsequent error id is paired with a different event's title/message/timestamp and the trailing errors are silently dropped, so the LLM summary reports the wrong errors against the wrong messages and omits real ones.

[BUG] gen_request_data compares error-event timestamps (epoch seconds from nodestore event payloads) against rrweb breadcrumb timestamps (epoch milliseconds in recording segments) as if they shared a unit, so error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0) is true for every breadcrumb. All error log lines are yielded before the first breadcrumb message, so the chronological interleaving that the docstring and this change promise is never produced and the Seer summary loses the temporal correlation between errors and user actions.

[BUG] The validation loop returns 422 for the entire batch when any single report fails the strict serializer (ChoiceField on the hardcoded 8-type BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES list plus required destination/user_agent/attempts), instead of skipping the invalid report and counting the valid siblings. The moment a browser ships a report type outside the hardcoded list (or sends a Working-Draft report lacking `destination`), every batch containing it is rejected wholesale, so this collector's per-type metrics silently drop to zero for the valid reports in those batches too, with no signal that data is being lost.

[BUG] MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE places the unescaped, unfiltered issue title inside markdown link text ([**{title}**]({url})), while the previous per-provider templates kept the title outside the link. Any issue title containing "]" (e.g. "[bug] Crash on login") terminates the link text early and renders a mangled GitHub/GitLab merged-PR comment with a broken View Issue link, a regression the old template did not have; _truncate_title does not escape brackets.

[ADVISORY] The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness (self.initial_data.get("age") / get("timestamp")) and both fields are required=False, so age:0 sent alongside timestamp and reports containing neither field pass validation. Spec-invalid reports (zero-valued or missing both fields) are accepted and counted as valid in browser_report metrics, skewing exactly the rollout data this collector exists to gather, and the next person debugging report handling cannot trust the 422 as evidence a payload was actually malformed.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint unconditionally executes the query_replay_instance snuba query (whose only consumer is the error-id fetch) even when enable_error_context=false, and the new error-context behavior is gated solely by a client-supplied query parameter with no feature flag or options entry. Operators have no server-side way to disable the newly added per-request snuba query plus nodestore multi-get on the summarize path without a code deploy, and clients that opt out still pay the full snuba query cost on every request.

[ADVISORY] get_environment_info adds an issue.get_recommended_event() call (eventstore lookup plus nodestore fetch) per issue inside the merged-PR comment-body loop, a path that previously built the comment purely from Group DB fields. Every GitHub/Gitlab merged-PR comment for orgs with the PR bot enabled now performs N remote eventstore/nodestore round-trips proportional to the number of linked issues, adding latency and backend load to the comment-posting task and a new failure source that, while caught, silently strips environment info from comments.

[ADVISORY] Removing the regex-experiment branch orphans _handle_regex_match (its only call site was the deleted else-branch) and leaves ParameterizationRegex exported in __all__ with its only subclass deleted, so the file retains a regex pipeline that can never execute. The next engineer touching grouping parameterization greps, finds a live-looking regex handler and exported regex class, and either wastes time wiring them up or builds a ParameterizationRegex subclass that the unconditionally-callback dispatch in run() will invoke with the wrong callback contract; deleting both removes the trap.

[ADVISORY] The autofix automation tuning default now lives in two independently hand-maintained places — DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT in constants.py and the literal default="off" in the sentry:autofix_automation_tuning register() call in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205 — which this diff had to update in parallel. The next default flip (the third in this key's short history) that updates only one site silently desynchronizes the constant read by API/validation code from the actually-registered project-option default, giving every default-on org a different automation behavior than the code elsewhere assumes.

[BUG] This 11-line null-segment guard is the only change in the entire src/sentry portion of the diff traceable to the PR's stated intent ('Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System'); every other backend change — the autofix default flip (constants.py:724, projectoptions/defaults.py:205), the neutered migrations 0917/0920, the browser-reporting collector rewrite, the GitHub/GitLab merged-PR comment feature, workflow-engine detector ownership, webhook/auth taskworker deadlines, ourlogs equations, preprod analytics, the feedback-summaries prompt rewrite, the grouping-experiment removal, and a large frontend Flex/UI migration — implements at least twelve unrelated subsystems with no bulk-delete requirement behind them. The changeset enforces no invariant connecting it to the titled system: there is no bulk-delete endpoint, model, permission, or task anywhere in the diff's backend, so the PR cannot be reviewed, tested, or reverted as the stated feature — reverting a bulk-delete regression silently reverts the autofix product flip, the migration neutering, and the rest of the unrelated bundle in the same deploy.

[BUG] The org-wide autofix automation default is flipped from "low" to "off" (with its twin registration flipped at src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205) inside a PR titled "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System". Every organization and project that never explicitly set sentry:autofix_automation_tuning silently stops running autofix automatically on new issues the moment this replays PR deploys, and a later revert of the bulk-delete work silently re-enables it — a product behavior change no replays reviewer or changelog accounts for.

[BUG] The migration body is replaced with a bare `return` that skips the org-saved-searches-to-views conversion entirely, deferring to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, which appears nowhere in this diff's fully-visible src/sentry/migrations section. Environments that deploy this PR without the absent 0921 replacement never convert organization saved searches into group-search views, permanently stranding that data, and the migration surgery is invisible to reviewers because it rides a PR titled for replays bulk delete.

[BUG] This already-shipped data migration is neutered to a bare `return` deferring to a 0921 replacement that is not part of this changeset, inside a PR whose stated intent is replays bulk delete. Any deployment taking this PR without the referenced 0921 migration permanently skips the org saved-search conversion, and reverting the unrelated replays work restores a migration body the comment itself calls erroneous, leaving operators with no consistent migration story.

[BUG] The new get_environment_info, _truncate_title, and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template helpers are added to CommitContextIntegration, but GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body (src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:406) and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body (src/sentry/integrations/gitlab/integration.py:254) invoke them via `self.` on PRCommentWorkflow instances, which subclass OpenPRCommentWorkflow — not CommitContextIntegration. Building any merged-PR comment raises AttributeError ('GitHubPRCommentWorkflow' object has no attribute 'get_merged_pr_single_issue_template'), so GitHub and GitLab merged-PR issue comments are never posted; the staticmethod's internal `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` reference is a second AttributeError on the same path, and this customer-facing integration break ships unreviewed inside a PR titled for replays bulk delete.

[BUG] A different replays feature — Snuba-sourced error context for AI breadcrumb summarization — is built inside the bulk-delete PR, adding an unconditional query_replay_instance Snuba call and a nodestore get_multi to a GET path that previously only paginated object-storage segment metadata. The bulk-delete ship is welded to an unrelated AI feature (reverting either reverts both), and the endpoint now fails closed during Snuba outages: query_replay_instance at line 70 is not wrapped in any try/except, so replay summarization 500s on a path that previously never touched Snuba.

[BUG] fetch_error_details copies the nodestore event's "timestamp" (an ISO-8601 string) verbatim into ErrorEvent despite the TypedDict declaring float, and gen_request_data compares it against replay breadcrumb events' numeric epoch timestamps. Any summarize-breadcrumbs request for a replay that has error events raises TypeError ('<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'float') while merging the chronological log stream, returning a 500 instead of the summary — the new error-context path crashes on exactly the replays it was built for.

[ADVISORY] A 20-service `tracing` dev profile — plus the new snuba-metrics service (lines 23-29), four subscription-results consumers, and four new consumer commands (lines 325-332) — is added to devservices inside a PR whose stated intent is replays bulk delete. Developers bringing up an environment to test bulk delete now spawn relay, six ingest consumers, three post-process forwarders, four subscription consumers, and a worker; any devservices breakage in this stack gets bisected to a replays commit, and the dev-infra expansion is unreviewable as bulk-delete work.

[ADVISORY] The browser-reporting collector's validation is rewritten from a dataclass to a DRF serializer with new rejection rules (attempts >= 1, age XOR timestamp, type whitelist) and a changed response contract (JSON error bodies on 422 where empty HttpResponse was returned), none of it traceable to the bulk-delete intent. A batch containing one invalid report is now rejected wholesale before the metrics loop (line ~106 early return), so valid reports in the same POST are never counted, and clients or tests pinned to the old empty-body responses break when this replays PR deploys — only on orgs with issues.browser_reporting.collector_endpoint_enabled.

[ADVISORY] A new detector-ownership API capability (owner = ActorField, plus owner_user_id/owner_team_id handling in create() at lines 119-134 and the owner-clearing branch in update() at lines 65-79) is implemented inside the bulk-delete PR. The workflow-engine API surface grows and reverts with unrelated replays code: an owner=None payload clears both owner columns through a branch no workflow-engine reviewer sees in context, and reverting the bulk-delete work silently strips the owner field from the public detector API.

[ADVISORY] The "Type" row and its explanatory QuestionTooltip are deleted from the grouping-info panel for the COMPONENT, CUSTOM_FINGERPRINT, BUILT_IN_FINGERPRINT, SALTED_COMPONENT, and PERFORMANCE_ISSUE variants — a user-facing information removal unrelated to replays bulk delete. Users and support engineers debugging issue grouping lose the variant-type label and its algorithm explanation after a replays deploy, with no requirement in the stated intent tracing the removal and no way to revert it without reverting bulk-delete code.

[ADVISORY] The AI summarization prompt is rewritten (55-word hard cap, two-sentence cap, "\n------\n" separators replacing the "- {msg}" bullet format) inside the replays bulk-delete PR. The feedback-summaries feature's input contract changes silently when this replays PR deploys — the model now consumes dash-delimited raw feedback text instead of bulleted lines — and any summarize regression gets entangled with a replays revert.

[ADVISORY] ParameterizationRegexExperiment is deleted and ParameterizationExperiment collapsed to the callable experiment, together with the removal of the grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option (src/sentry/options/defaults.py:2627) — grouping-engine surgery untraceable to the bulk-delete intent. Grouping configs that still name the removed experiment type silently lose that parameterization path, and environments holding stored values for the deleted option key are left with unregistered-option configuration; the removal reverts (resurrecting the experiment mid-stream) with unrelated replays code.

[ADVISORY] Hard processing deadlines (30s for schedule_webhook_delivery, 300s for drain_mailbox, 120s for drain_mailbox_parallel) are added to webhook taskworker configs inside the replays bulk-delete PR. Webhook delivery tasks gain kill timers nobody reviewed in the context of webhooks: if 30s proves too tight for large organizations, schedule_webhook_delivery tasks are killed mid-run after this replays deploys, and retuning the value requires touching unrelated replays code.

[ADVISORY] check_auth_identities gains a 60-second processing_deadline_duration inside the replays bulk-delete PR. Auth identity checks exceeding 60s are killed once this unrelated PR deploys, and a replays revert silently removes the deadline again — the tuning is invisible to both the auth owners and the replays reviewers.

[ADVISORY] An `equations` parameter is threaded through run_top_events_timeseries_query, extending the logs analytics query API inside the replays bulk-delete PR. The logs query surface grows inside an unrelated changeset with no requirement behind it; any caller adopting equations is silently broken when a replays revert removes the parameter.

[ADVISORY] DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType gains noise_config = NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5), changing when this security issue type surfaces its alerts, inside the bulk-delete PR. Organizations begin seeing suppressed early occurrences of DB-query-injection security issues after an unrelated replays deploy, and reverting the replays work silently reverts security-issue tuning no security reviewer signed off on in context.

[ADVISORY] A new preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event (registered in src/sentry/preprod/analytics.py, exported via the new wildcard import in src/sentry/preprod/__init__.py) is recorded in the assemble endpoint inside the bulk-delete PR — and the record call fires before the features.has gate. Requests from organizations without the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble flag (which the endpoint 404s) still emit assemble analytics, polluting the new metric from day one, and the instrumentation ships and reverts with unrelated replays code.

[ADVISORY] A frontend refactor wave — replacing hand-rolled FlexSpacer/FlexContainer styled divs with the core Flex component across codeSnippet, branchSelector, dateSelector, integratedOrgSelector, repoSelector, eventAttachments, and newTraceDetailsHeader, plus a chonk button transition change from 0.1s to 0.06s (styles.chonk.tsx:113) — ships inside the replays bulk-delete PR. Layout regressions in codecov selectors, attachment tables, and code snippets get bisected to replays commits, and reverting bulk-delete reverts UI polish across six unrelated components; none of it traces to the stated intent.

[ADVISORY] The delayed-workflow processor is restructured — slow conditions fetched once and threaded through get_condition_query_groups/get_groups_to_fire, a new no_slow_condition_groups info log, an event_data-to-workflow_event_data logging fix (line 583), and a log_context logger swap in src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/workflow.py:35 — inside the bulk-delete PR. A regression in this refactor breaks workflow firing for every org while riding a PR titled for replays bulk delete; the workflow-engine change is invisible to workflow-engine reviewers and reverts alongside unrelated replays code.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs each event_id with nodestore payload data via zip(error_ids, events.values()), but nodestore.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits missing nodes and (on the Django backend) iterates an unordered queryset, so the values() stream is not aligned with error_ids. Whenever any requested node id is missing (retention expiry, deleted event) or the backend returns rows in other than input order, every ErrorEvent after the first omission carries a different event's id, title, message, and timestamp; the replay-summarize prompt then attributes one error's details to the wrong error id, producing wrong AI summaries with no error raised anywhere.

[BUG] The chronological merge in gen_request_data compares error timestamps read raw from nodestore event payloads (Sentry event timestamps: RFC3339 strings or epoch seconds) against rrweb segment-event timestamps (epoch milliseconds), and no unit or type normalization is performed anywhere in the diff. The comparison error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0) either raises TypeError ('<' between 'str' and 'int') and 500s the previously-working summarize endpoint on every replay that has errors, or — when both values are numeric — epoch-seconds always compare less than epoch-milliseconds so every error drains before the first breadcrumb and the interleaved chronological error context this diff was built to produce never appears.

[BUG] The age/timestamp validators enforce only mutual exclusion via truthiness checks on initial_data (self.initial_data.get('age') / get('timestamp')), so a report containing neither field — and a report whose excluded field is 0 — passes validation, contradicting the one-of shape both validators' docstrings assert and both Reporting API specs require. Malformed reports the author's own contract says must be rejected are accepted and counted in browser_reporting.raw_report_received metrics, and an age=0-plus-timestamp (or timestamp=0-plus-age) pair bypasses the mutual exclusion entirely, so the collected metrics and any downstream parsing silently include spec-invalid payloads.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint executes the full query_replay_instance snuba query and process_raw_response before evaluating the enable_error_context opt-out flag, so the flag only skips the nodestore fetch while the snuba round-trip — whose only consumer is error_ids — still runs. Clients that pass enable_error_context=false, and every request for a replay with no errors, still pay a per-request replay-instance snuba query, adding snuba load and latency the flag promises to eliminate; the fix requires moving the check above query_replay_instance.

[ADVISORY] Error extraction routes through process_raw_response with the client-controlled `field` query param and then reads response[0].get('error_ids', []), so the server-side error-context feature functions only when the caller happens to include 'error_ids' in its field list. A summarize caller that omits field=error_ids gets error_events == [] from the silent .get fallback with no log or error, shipping summaries with zero error context that are indistinguishable from replays without errors — a hidden client/server coupling that makes the feature fail silently.

[ADVISORY] The new error-context path guards only the nodestore fetch (fetch_error_details wraps everything in a broad except that degrades to an empty list) while the equally-optional snuba dependency query_replay_instance immediately above it is left unguarded. A snuba outage or slow query — a dependency this endpoint never had before this diff — now 500s the entire breadcrumbs-summarize endpoint, even though the author's own nodestore handling demonstrates the error context was meant to degrade gracefully; the previously snuba-independent summary path is taken down by an optional enrichment.

[ADVISORY] get_comment_body calls self.get_environment_info(issue) inside the comprehension over issues, and get_environment_info issues issue.get_recommended_event() (group-hash lookup plus nodestore read) and environment resolution per issue with no batching. Every merged-PR comment now performs roughly 2-3 extra queries plus a nodestore fetch per issue (up to 5 issues per PR), adding avoidable per-issue latency and nodestore load to a comment path that previously issued zero per-issue lookups.

[ADVISORY] get_comment_body calls self.get_environment_info(issue) inside the comprehension over issues, and get_environment_info issues issue.get_recommended_event() (group-hash lookup plus nodestore read) and environment resolution per issue with no batching. Every merged-PR comment now performs roughly 2-3 extra queries plus a nodestore fetch per issue (up to 5 issues per PR), adding avoidable per-issue latency and nodestore load to a comment path that previously issued zero per-issue lookups.

[ADVISORY] Switching url validation from the untyped dataclass to serializers.URLField() imposes Django's http/https/ftp(s)-only scheme whitelist on a field the previous code accepted as any string. A batch containing one report whose url is about:blank, file://, or a chrome-extension:// page is now rejected wholesale with 422, and since browsers fire-and-forget report deliveries, those reports are never ingested or counted — a silent ingestion regression relative to the previous accept-anything behavior.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint records the preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event as the first statement of post(), before the feature-gate check (and before any payload validation), with no outcome attribute distinguishing accepted from rejected requests. Requests from organizations lacking the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble flag, and requests that subsequently fail validation, are recorded as assemble operations, so dashboards and alerts on this event measure gated-out demand rather than actual assembles and cannot be interpreted either way.

[ADVISORY] The autofix tuning default is maintained as two independent literals — DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT in src/sentry/constants.py line 724 and the hardcoded default="off" in this project-option registration — with no single source of truth. This diff itself had to perform the same low->off edit in two files in lockstep; the next tuning change that edits only one location leaves the org-level default and the project-level default silently diverged, producing different autofix behavior per scope with no test failing.

[ADVISORY] Narrowing ParameterizationExperiment to ParameterizationCallableExperiment and deleting the isinstance dispatch leaves the regex-experiment machinery behind — ParameterizationRegex is still defined and exported in __all__ and _handle_regex_match is now uncalled — while Parameterizer.run unconditionally passes the (str, int) -> None counting callback to every experiment. Any code that still constructs the exported ParameterizationRegex class receives _incr_counter where its run contract expects a (re.Match) -> str regex-sub callback and raises TypeError mid-grouping; meanwhile the dead callback helper and the dual callback contracts force the next reader to reason about an experiment kind that can no longer legitimately occur — the deletion should have removed _handle_regex_match and the regex path entirely.

[BUG] A reports array containing any non-object element (e.g. [null], ["x"], [42]) crashes serializer.is_valid() with an uncaught TypeError, because DRF's Serializer.to_internal_value raises TypeError (not ValidationError) for non-Mapping data and is_valid() only catches ValidationError. An anonymous client (permission_classes is empty on this CORS-enabled endpoint) POSTs [null] while issues.browser_reporting.collector_endpoint_enabled is on, and the request returns a 500 with an unhandled TypeError instead of the 422 the newly added validation path exists to return, flooding error tracking and defeating the rewrite's stated purpose for exactly this malformed-input class.

[BUG] The new Snuba query_replay_instance call runs unconditionally before the enable_error_context=false check even though its only consumed output is error_ids, so the disable flag fails to gate the query it was introduced to gate. Every summarize-breadcrumbs request pays an extra Snuba query even when the client explicitly disabled error context, and the endpoint — which previously depended only on segment storage — now returns 500 whenever the replays Snuba query raises, breaking breadcrumb summarization entirely during Snuba incidents instead of degrading to the flag's intended no-error-context path.

[BUG] Replacing FlexCenter (which applied the overflowEllipsis theme mixin, i.e. overflow:hidden, on the flex container) with <Flex align="center"> removes the only overflow clamp on the attachment-name cell, so the ellipsized Name no longer shrinks (flex children default to min-width:auto) and long names overflow the 1fr grid column. Attachments with long file names stop ellipsizing after this refactor and their text bleeds into the Size/Actions columns of the panel table, a visual regression that short-named fixtures will not catch.

[ADVISORY] BrowserReportSerializer accepts reports containing neither age nor timestamp (both are required=False and each cross-field validator only runs when its own field is present), so the exactly-one-of constraint that the validators' docstrings ("Validate that age is present", "timestamp is present") and the spec comments claim to enforce is not implemented. Spec-violating reports with no time field are validated and counted in browser_reporting.raw_report_received, so anyone using this collector for real ingestion inherits unageable records and the validation rewrite's own stated contract is silently unenforced.

[ADVISORY] Error context extraction reads error_ids from process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field")), so error events come back empty unless the client happens to include error_ids in a field query param this endpoint never consumed before. Any existing caller of summarize-breadcrumbs that does not pass field=error_ids gets zero error context with no error and no log, so the headline feature of this change silently no-ops for them while appearing to work in tests that pass the magic param.

[ADVISORY] Deleting the grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option registration (along with the ParameterizationRegexExperiment class in parameterization.py) silently reverts the traceparent parameterization experiment for every project that has the option set to a non-zero rate, with no migration, flag-down sequence, or rollout-verified zero stated. Projects mid-rollout stop parameterizing traceparent strings at deploy; their grouping fingerprints change, so subsequent events hash to new fingerprints and existing issues fork into duplicate groups — the high-blast-radius regrouping that the option's FLAG_RATE rollout machinery existed to prevent, shipped inside a PR whose stated objective is replays bulk deletion.

[ADVISORY] DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT flips from "low" to "off", silently disabling autofix automation for every organization relying on the default, inside a PR about replays bulk deletion. After deploy, projects without an explicit sentry:autofix_automation_tuning setting stop running autofix on new issues with no migration or product-accepted flag-off; users lose an accepted, previously-shipped behavior they never opted out of, and the only evidence of the decision is a one-line default flip in an unrelated diff.

[ADVISORY] The project option default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning flips from "low" to "off", contradicting the option's own registration comment ("Should autofix run automatically on new issues") by making the answer "never" for all default-reliant projects. Every project that inherits this default stops auto-running autofix on new issues at deploy time; the behavior change is invisible to admins because it ships as a default flip buried in a replays PR rather than an opt-out option or migration.

[ADVISORY] The merged-PR issue comment format changes from "- ‼️ **{title}** `{culprit}` [View Issue]({url})" to "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}", dropping the culprit subtitle entirely and truncating titles at 50 characters, silently altering the output of the already-shipped GitHub/GitLab PR bot. Orgs with sentry:github_pr_bot or sentry:gitlab_pr_bot enabled see merged-PR comments lose the culprit context and long issue titles cut mid-word after this deploy, with no feature flag to preserve the previously accepted comment format.

[ADVISORY] get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() once per issue inside the get_comment_body loop, adding a nodestore/eventstore fetch for every issue in every generated merged-PR comment where the previous code used only DB columns (issue.title, issue.culprit). Every merged-PR comment now performs up to N extra remote event fetches before posting, adding latency and backend load to the PR-bot path; and because the broad `except Exception` swallows failures, the environment info silently disappears whenever those fetches fail, with no way to distinguish 'no environment' from 'fetch broken'.

[ADVISORY] analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...) fires before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature gate and before any payload validation, so rejected and invalid requests are recorded as assemble events. The preprod_artifact.api.assemble event overcounts assembles with gated-off attempts and malformed requests, skewing any adoption/funnel analysis built on it, and users in gated-off orgs emit user_id-bearing analytics for requests the endpoint immediately rejects.

[BUG] ActorField resolves user:/team: identifiers globally with no organization-membership scoping, and the serializer's create() and update() persist the resolved id directly into owner_user_id/owner_team_id, so a user with detector-write access can assign any foreign-org user or team as a detector owner by POSTing owner: "user:<arbitrary id>". adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results via zip(error_ids, events.values()), but nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict containing only the node ids that were found, so the two sequences misalign whenever any error event is missing from nodestore. For any replay where at least one error event has been purged from nodestore (retention, deletion), every subsequent error id is paired with a different event's title/message/timestamp and the trailing errors are silently dropped, so the LLM summary reports the wrong errors against the wrong messages and omits real ones.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then constructs results with `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Since `get_multi` returns a dict of found results (and can omit missing node_ids), `events.values()` will not have a 1:1 positional correspondence with `error_ids` when any event is missing, causing mis-pairing and truncation. The correct approach would index by node_id (or iterate `error_ids` and look up `events.get(node_id)`), not zip with `values()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] gen_request_data compares error-event timestamps (epoch seconds from nodestore event payloads) against rrweb breadcrumb timestamps (epoch milliseconds in recording segments) as if they shared a unit, so error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0) is true for every breadcrumb. All error log lines are yielded before the first breadcrumb message, so the chronological interleaving that the docstring and this change promise is never produced and the Seer summary loses the temporal correlation between errors and user actions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `error_events[*]["timestamp"]` coming from `nodestore` event payloads and `event.get("timestamp", 0)` coming from decoded replay segment JSON, but it does not establish that replay/breadcrumb timestamps are epoch milliseconds. In fact, the updated unit test `test_get_request_data` uses breadcrumb timestamps `1.5` and `2.0` and error timestamps `1.0` and `3.0`, implying the code expects both to be comparable in the same unit (seconds) and validates correct interleaving. Therefore the claim that the comparison is always true due to seconds-vs-milliseconds mismatch is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The validation loop returns 422 for the entire batch when any single report fails the strict serializer (ChoiceField on the hardcoded 8-type BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES list plus required destination/user_agent/attempts), instead of skipping the invalid report and counting the valid siblings. The moment a browser ships a report type outside the hardcoded list (or sends a Working-Draft report lacking `destination`), every batch containing it is rejected wholesale, so this collector's per-type metrics silently drop to zero for the valid reports in those batches too, with no signal that data is being lost.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, the code validates reports in a loop and immediately returns `Response(..., 422)` on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(...)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details pairs each event_id with nodestore payload data via zip(error_ids, events.values()), but nodestore.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits missing nodes and (on the Django backend) iterates an unordered queryset, so the values() stream is not aligned with error_ids. Whenever any requested node id is missing (retention expiry, deleted event) or the backend returns rows in other than input order, every ErrorEvent after the first omission carries a different event's id, title, message, and timestamp; the replay-summarize prompt then attributes one error's details to the wrong error id, producing wrong AI summaries with no error raised anywhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The chronological merge in gen_request_data compares error timestamps read raw from nodestore event payloads (Sentry event timestamps: RFC3339 strings or epoch seconds) against rrweb segment-event timestamps (epoch milliseconds), and no unit or type normalization is performed anywhere in the diff. The comparison error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0) either raises TypeError ('<' between 'str' and 'int') and 500s the previously-working summarize endpoint on every replay that has errors, or — when both values are numeric — epoch-seconds always compare less than epoch-milliseconds so every error drains before the first breadcrumb and the interleaved chronological error context this diff was built to produce never appears.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The age/timestamp validators enforce only mutual exclusion via truthiness checks on initial_data (self.initial_data.get('age') / get('timestamp')), so a report containing neither field — and a report whose excluded field is 0 — passes validation, contradicting the one-of shape both validators' docstrings assert and both Reporting API specs require. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ActorField resolves user:/team: identifiers globally with no organization-membership scoping, and the serializer's create() and update() persist the resolved id directly into owner_user_id/owner_team_id, so a user with detector-write access can assign any foreign-org user or team as a detector owner by POSTing owner: "user:<arbitrary id>". A member of org A sets the owner of a detector in org A to a user id belonging to org B (ActorField's global lookup accepts it, and both the update path at lines 67-79 and the create path at lines 120-136 write owner.id with no org check); valid ids are accepted while invalid ones return a validation error, enabling cross-tenant user/team id enumeration, and the foreign user's display name/email is then resolved and rendered in org A's detector views while any owner-based routing points at an outsider — a cross-tenant identity disclosure and tenant-isolation break.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)` being added and the create/update paths persisting `owner.id` into `owner_user_id/owner_team_id`. However, the finding’s core claim (ActorField resolves actors “globally” with no organization-membership scoping, enabling cross-tenant assignment/enumeration) is not supported by the diff. ActorField’s lookup/validation behavior is not shown here, and the added endpoint tests explicitly assert that an owner from another organization is rejected with a 400 (`test_owner_not_in_organization` in `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/test_organization_detector_index.py`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a logging sink that writes the raw, unvalidated browser report (raw_report) verbatim to logs on an endpoint with permission_classes = (), @csrf_exempt, and @allow_cors_options, which (together with the unconditional browser_report_received info log at line 93 that dumps the full request body on every POST) persists fully attacker-controlled bodies into log storage with no authentication or scrubbing. Anyone on the internet can POST arbitrary JSON to this collector and have it written to info/warning-level logs; because Browser Reporting API payloads include the url field carrying the reporting page's full URL with query-string PII (emails, session tokens, user ids), end-user PII lands in ops logs that lack the scrubbing applied to event data, and the unauthenticated endpoint doubles as a log-flooding/cost vector whenever issues.browser_reporting.collector_endpoint_enabled is turned on.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post` the code logs fully attacker-controlled request content: an unconditional `logger.info("browser_report_received", extra={"request_body": request.data})` occurs before any validation/scrubbing, and the new validation failure path adds `logger.warning(... extra={"validation_errors": serializer.errors, "raw_report": report})` which also persists the raw report. The endpoint is unauthenticated (`permission_classes = ()`) and `@csrf_exempt`/`@allow_cors_options` make it broadly reachable, so this is a real security/privacy and log-flooding vector when the option is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details copies the raw nodestore payload's timestamp — an ISO-8601 string, while the .get default 0.0 is a float — into ErrorEvent['timestamp'], which get_request_data/gen_request_data then compare against the numeric timestamps of replay breadcrumb events. With error context enabled (the default), every summarize-breadcrumbs request for a replay that has errors raises TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'float' at the first interleaved breadcrumb (or earlier in error_events.sort when one error lacks a timestamp), turning the endpoint into a 500 instead of returning the summary; a test seeding nodestore with float timestamps passes while production payloads crash.

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py, fetch_error_details assigns ErrorEvent['timestamp'] directly from nodestore payload via data.get("timestamp", 0.0) without coercion/validation, even though ErrorEvent declares timestamp: float. Later, get_request_data sorts error_events by x["timestamp"] and gen_request_data compares error timestamp against breadcrumb event timestamps (floats) using '<'. If nodestore returns a non-numeric timestamp (e.g., a string), this will raise at sort time or during the '<' comparison, turning the endpoint into a 500 when error context is enabled. The diff introduces this new interleaving logic without ensuring consistent timestamp types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details pairs each event_id with the i-th element of events.values() via zip, but nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits missing keys and iterates in backend order, so the i-th value is not the i-th error's data (and the `if data is not None` filter never fires because absent keys are simply missing, not None-valued). Whenever any of the replay's error events is missing from nodestore or get_multi returns keys in other than input order, error A's title/message/timestamp are attributed to error B's id and fed into the chronological interleave and Seer prompt, silently producing a misattributed AI summary with no exception raised; a single-error test cannot catch this.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new code in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), it builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then constructs results by `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Because `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id, the returned dict may omit missing node_ids and `values()` is not tied to the original `error_ids` list. If any event is missing (or if ordering differs), `zip` will pair an `event_id` with the wrong event data (or drop some entirely), silently misattributing error details in the Seer prompt. The `if data is not None` guard also won't catch missing entries because missing keys won't appear in `events.values()` at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update() writes instance.owner_user_id = owner.id / instance.owner_team_id = owner.id where owner is the Actor row returned by ActorField, so it stores the Actor table's primary key rather than the user id (owner.user_id) or team id (owner.team_id) that the owner_user_id/owner_team_id columns reference. [BUG] create() derives owner_user_id/owner_team_id from owner.id — the Actor row's primary key resolved by ActorField — instead of owner.user_id/owner.team_id, the values the detector's owner_user_id/owner_team_id columns hold. adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, `owner` is introduced as `owner = ActorField(...)` and then handled via `owner.is_user` / `owner.is_team` with `owner.id` assigned into `owner_user_id` / `owner_team_id` (in both `update()` and `create()`). Additionally, new tests added in this diff explicitly validate that setting `owner` results in `detector.owner_user_id == self.user.id` and `detector.owner_team_id == team.id`, which directly contradicts the alleged behavior.

Given only what’s shown in the diff, the asserted IntegrityError / wrong-ID storage is not verifiable and is contradicted by the added tests’ intended contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The GET handler now unconditionally runs query_replay_instance and process_raw_response on every request, and the enable_error_context=false escape hatch only skips fetch_error_details, so the new Snuba query — whose exceptions are unhandled — still executes on a path that previously never touched Snuba. adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the diff adds an unconditional Snuba fetch via `query_replay_instance(...)` and `process_raw_response(...)` before checking `enable_error_context` (which only gates `fetch_error_details`). There is no try/except around the Snuba call/processing, so a Snuba outage/exception would now bubble up and fail the request even when `enable_error_context=false`. The previous implementation (removed at the bottom of the file) only iterated blob segments via `iter_segment_data` and did not touch Snuba. This is a real reliability/architecture regression introduced by the change, even if not a strict functional correctness defect in normal conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] validate_timestamp/validate_age enforce only mutual exclusion using falsy checks (self.initial_data.get('age') / get('timestamp')), so a report containing neither age nor timestamp — or pairing one with the other set to 0 — passes validation although both spec variants require exactly one of the two fields. Spec-invalid reports clear the validation gate this diff adds and increment browser_reporting.raw_report_received, so anyone relying on the endpoint to filter malformed payloads, or on that metric for report volume, gets quietly inflated counts.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, and the per-field validators only attempt mutual exclusion via falsy checks: `validate_timestamp` does `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` does `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. This (a) allows reports with neither `age` nor `timestamp` to pass validation, and (b) allows both to be present when the “other” is `0` (since `0` is falsy), so spec-invalid payloads can pass the new validation gate. The endpoint then increments `browser_reporting.raw_report_received` for each validated report, so these invalid-but-accepted reports will inflate the metric as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BrowserReportSerializer marks user_agent, destination, and attempts (IntegerField(min_value=1)) as required, which rejects Working-Draft reports (type/url/age/body only, per the spec the new 'We need to support both' comment claims to support) and any report carrying attempts: 0. Reporting-API Working-Draft clients, whose reports lack user_agent/destination/attempts, and browsers that send attempts: 0 on first delivery receive 422 for the entire batch, so the collector never records those reports despite the dual-spec support the comment promises.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, both the serializer and the added tests treat `user_agent`, `destination`, and `attempts` as required fields for the “Working Draft” format: `DEPRECATION_REPORT` (commented as Working Draft) includes all three, and tests assert 422 when required fields (e.g., `user_agent`) are missing and when `attempts` is 0. The claim that Working-Draft clients send only `{type,url,age,body}` and that browsers send `attempts: 0` is not supported by the diff; it relies on external spec/behavior assumptions not evidenced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Replacing FlexCenter with <Flex align="center"> drops the container's theme.overflowEllipsis (overflow:hidden), which was the load-bearing clip that set the 1fr grid cell's automatic minimum size to 0 and let long attachment names ellipsize. An attachment filename wider than its column no longer ellipsizes — the nowrap Name flex child cannot shrink below its min-content width — so the name bleeds out of the panel row and collides with the Size and actions columns.

adjudication.rationale: In `static/app/components/events/eventAttachments.tsx`, the first grid cell wrapper was changed from `FlexCenter` (a styled `div` that applied `p.theme.overflowEllipsis`, i.e. overflow clipping) to `<Flex align="center">` with no overflow styling. In CSS grid (`grid-template-columns: 1fr auto auto`), a grid item with `overflow: hidden` typically allows the item to shrink below its min-content size; removing that can cause the 1fr cell to not shrink and let long, `white-space: nowrap` content overflow into adjacent columns. `Name` has overflowEllipsis, but it is now a flex child inside the grid item and does not set `min-width: 0`, so the wrapper losing overflow clipping can indeed break ellipsis/layout.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This hunk removes the only call site of _handle_regex_match (the regex-experiment callback) yet leaves the private helper and the ParameterizationRegex base class — still exported in __all__ — in place after deleting their only subclass ParameterizationRegexExperiment. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] get_environment_info wraps the entire environment lookup in a bare `except Exception` that logs at info level and returns '', swallowing every failure mode — including programming errors inside this newly added method — behind a silent degradation. A defect in the recommended-event/environment lookup (TypeError, AttributeError, malformed data) ships silently: merged-PR comments just lose their environment suffix with only an info-level breadcrumb, and nothing alerts anyone that the new feature is dead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info` which wraps the whole lookup in `try: ... except Exception as e:` and on any exception logs `logger.info(...)` then returns an empty string (no environment suffix). This behavior is explicit in the new code (comment: "If anything goes wrong, just continue without environment info"), so it’s not a verifiable correctness defect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/observability concern: unexpected programming/data errors in the new environment-lookup path will be swallowed and only produce an info-level log while silently degrading PR comment output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The chronological merge in gen_request_data compares error-event timestamps copied verbatim from nodestore payloads (epoch-seconds floats, or the 0.0 default when the key is absent) against RRWeb replay-segment event timestamps (epoch milliseconds), so error_events[...]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0) mixes different units and is true for every pair, yielding every error message before every breadcrumb instead of at its chronological position. The Seer summarize-breadcrumbs prompt always receives all error messages at the head of the log, detached from the breadcrumbs surrounding them, so AI summaries misstate when errors occurred; if any nodestore payload stores its timestamp as an ISO string (or a missing key injects the 0.0 float default into error_events.sort), the comparison raises TypeError and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of a summary.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `gen_request_data` merge logic (`src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), the diff provides no evidence that replay-segment event timestamps are epoch-milliseconds while nodestore event timestamps are epoch-seconds. In fact, the updated tests use float timestamps in seconds for replay events (e.g. `1.5`, `2.0`, `float(now.timestamp())`) and for stored error events (`now.timestamp() - 1`), which are consistent units and contradict the finding’s “ms vs s” claim. The diff also doesn’t show any nodestore timestamps being ISO strings; while lack of casting could be a potential concern in general, the finding asserts a specific, always-broken behavior that is not supported by (and is partially contradicted by) the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids positionally with events.values() from nodestore.backend.get_multi, but get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits nodes it cannot find (and builds the dict in backend row order, not requested order), so whenever a requested error node is missing the ErrorEvent for one id is constructed from a different event's data. For any replay with at least one missing and one present error event (e.g. an event expired from nodestore while the replay row remains), the wrong title/message/timestamp is attributed to each error id and fed into the Seer summary, so the AI summary reports errors the user never hit and feeds wrong timestamps into the already broken chronological merge.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details` does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds results with `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Since `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id (and may omit missing nodes), iterating `events.values()` is not guaranteed to be in the same order/length as `error_ids`. If any node is missing (or ordering differs), the positional zip can associate an `event_id` with the wrong event data (or drop trailing ids), producing incorrect title/message/timestamp for a given error id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Replacing the body of the already-shipped 0917 migration with a no-op rests solely on the in-code comment 'was never run', but 0917 only errored on ownerless organization saved searches (the exact condition 0920's added owner_id__isnull=False filter was correcting), so any self-hosted install that upgraded while 0917 was live and had no such rows applied it successfully and recorded it in django_migrations. On those installs the replacement 0921 re-runs the conversion against GroupSearchView rows users have since edited, renamed, or deleted, resetting query/query_sort/date_added to the stale SavedSearch values and resurrecting deleted or renamed views — user data is silently overwritten with no rollback, and the migration file they applied no longer contains the operation that produced their data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both `0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py` were changed from performing data backfills (`SavedSearch` -> `GroupSearchView` via `update_or_create`) to unconditional no-ops (`return`) with only an in-code comment claiming they were never run. Rewriting an already-numbered migration like this breaks Django migration invariants: any deployment that previously applied 0917/0920 will have those migrations recorded in `django_migrations`, but the migration file contents no longer reflect the operations that created/updated data. This can lead to inconsistent states across installs and sets the stage for later “replacement” migrations to reapply or conflict with prior data migrations, risking silent overwrites/resurrections of user-edited `GroupSearchView` rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same no-op rewrite is applied to shipped migration 0920 (the owner_id__isnull=False-corrected version of the identical conversion), so the safety of skipping the conversion here again depends entirely on the undocumented claim that no database anywhere — developer machines, CI, self-hosted installs that upgraded during its live window — ever applied it before its error was identified. Any environment that did apply 0920 has the conversion recorded as done under pre-0921 semantics, and when 0921 runs it will update_or_create over user-modified GroupSearchView rows, resetting edited queries and re-creating views the user has since deleted or renamed from the still-present SavedSearch rows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows migrations 0917 and 0920 were changed to immediate no-ops with comments claiming they “had an error and was never run.” However, the finding’s core claim depends on facts not present in the diff: whether 0920 was ever shipped/applied anywhere and what 0921 actually does (e.g., whether it uses update_or_create in a way that would overwrite user-edited GroupSearchView rows). Since 0921’s implementation and any evidence of 0920 being applied are not shown here, the alleged data-overwrite behavior cannot be verified from this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template, get_environment_info and _truncate_title are defined on CommitContextIntegration, but the method body dereferences PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title — a class whose MRO (PRCommentWorkflow -> OpenPRCommentWorkflow -> ABC) never includes CommitContextIntegration — and the only callers (GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body in the integration.py diffs) invoke them via self. on workflow instances that equally lack these attributes. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] gen_request_data compares error-event timestamps taken verbatim from nodestore payloads (ISO-8601 strings like '2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', or epoch seconds if numeric) against rrweb breadcrumb timestamps (epoch-millisecond numbers) with '<' in the while-condition, and get_request_data sorts the same un-normalized values — no type or unit conversion happens anywhere in the pipeline. str < int raises TypeError and the summarize-breadcrumbs endpoint returns a 500 on every replay that has error events while error context is enabled (the default); in the numeric case every error is emitted before every breadcrumb and the chronological ordering the code promises is silently wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details()` copies `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` from nodestore into `ErrorEvent["timestamp"]` without any type/unit normalization, and `gen_request_data()` both sorts on that value and compares it with rrweb event `event.get("timestamp", 0)` using `<`. If nodestore returns a string timestamp (or if rrweb timestamps are ms while event timestamps are seconds), this can raise `TypeError` or produce chronologically wrong ordering. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details reads title and message as top-level keys of the event node payload (data.get("title", ""), data.get("message", "")), but error-event payloads carry the human-readable text under logentry and the title under the metadata object, so neither top-level key exists and both default to empty strings for every error. Every error line injected into the Seer prompt reads "User experienced an error: ': ' at <timestamp>", so the summarizer is fed empty error context while the endpoint returns 200 — the new error-context feature produces garbage for all real replays.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `fetch_error_details` reading `data.get("title")` and `data.get("message")`, but the claim that “error-event payloads” never have these top-level keys (only `logentry` / `metadata`) is not verifiable from the PR. In fact, the newly added replay summarize tests store an event with only an `exception` and then assert the Seer prompt contains `ZeroDivisionError` and `division by zero`; that would fail if the nodestore payload didn’t provide usable top-level `title`/`message` (or equivalents) for `fetch_error_details` to read. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] url = serializers.URLField() inherits DRF's default max_length=200, so any report whose document URL exceeds 200 characters fails validation and the post handler returns 422 for the entire batch on the first invalid report. Browsers fire-and-forget their reports and never surface collector 4xx responses, so pages with URLs longer than 200 characters (long query strings) never have their reports collected — silent data loss with no signal anywhere except the validation-failed log.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces strict validation in `BrowserReportSerializer` and uses `url = serializers.URLField()` with no explicit `max_length` (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py). DRF’s `URLField` enforces a maximum length (commonly 200 by default), so longer page/report URLs would be rejected and the endpoint returns `422` for the entire request on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(..., 422)`), causing silent drop of browser fire-and-forget reports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] validate_timestamp and validate_age enforce the age/timestamp mutual-exclusion contract with truthiness checks (self.initial_data.get("age") and .get("timestamp")), so a report carrying both fields where one is 0 — a legal value, timestamp even declares min_value=0 — is treated as having only one field and passes validation, and a report carrying neither field also passes because presence is never checked. Spec-violating reports (both age and timestamp present with one zero, or neither present) are accepted, counted in the browser_report_type metrics, and logged as valid data, corrupting the exact collection this serializer was added to guarantee.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, both `age` and `timestamp` are optional (`required=False`). The mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `.get("timestamp")`), so a value of `0` is treated as “absent”. That means a payload including both fields where one (or both) is `0` can incorrectly pass these validators. Additionally, there is no validation that *at least one* of `age` or `timestamp` is present, so a report with neither also validates. The endpoint then treats these as validated reports and increments `browser_reporting.raw_report_received` metrics based on `type`, as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs error IDs to event payloads positionally, which only stays correct if nodestore get_multi returns an input-ordered mapping with a None placeholder for every requested id and error_ids contains no duplicates — the code filters on data is not None but never looks payloads up by their node-id key (events[node_id]). On any get_multi backend that omits missing keys (retention-deleted events) or for a replay whose error_ids contains a duplicate event id, every pairing after the first gap shifts and one event's title/timestamp is attributed to a different error, silently misordering the error context fed to the summarizer.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), the code does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds results with `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. This assumes `events.values()` is in the same positional order as the input `node_ids` and that missing/duplicate IDs don’t change the mapping size/order. But `get_multi` returns a mapping keyed by node_id, and if it omits missing keys (or duplicates collapse to one dict key), `events.values()` can be shorter and/or ordered differently, causing subsequent `event_id` values to be paired with the wrong payload and silently attributing title/timestamp/message to the wrong error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] query_replay_instance and process_raw_response run unconditionally at the top of every request to this paginated endpoint, and the enable_error_context=false opt-out only skips the nodestore fetch — the snuba replay query executes even for error-context-disabled callers and re-executes identically on every page request although its result is constant for a given replay. Summarizing an N-page replay issues N identical snuba replay queries (plus up to N nodestore multi-gets) for constant data, adding a snuba roundtrip of latency to every page of the summarize flow and multiplying snuba load by page count.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code always computes `filter_params`, calls `query_replay_instance(...)`, and runs `process_raw_response(...)` before checking `enable_error_context` (the opt-out only gates `fetch_error_details(...)`). adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, the new `get_environment_info` wraps all logic in `except Exception as e:` and then logs via `logger.info("get_environment_info.no-environment", extra={"issue_id": issue.id, "error": e})` before returning "". This is diff-grounded: it will treat any unexpected failure (e.g., `issue.get_recommended_event()` / `get_environment()` changes or backend outages) as a routine info log, and it does not capture a traceback (no `logger.exception` / `exc_info=True` / Sentry capture). That makes missing environment enrichment hard to triage, but it is primarily an observability/operational concern rather than a functional bug since the method is explicitly designed to degrade gracefully.
